heard: A piece of the moon's blinding face is sitting in Madagascar. Looking up from Earth, the bright lunar highlands visible without a telescope are made of anorthosite. Over four billion years ago, light minerals floated on a magma ocean to form the moon's crust. Apollo astronauts hauled back tiny fragments, forcing researchers to hunt for larger rock analogs on Earth. While smaller deposits sit in Montana, Southern Madagascar holds an exposure of unprecedented scale. Astronauts aboard the space station photographed a brilliant, 40-square-mile white circle blazing against the landscape. Formed 600 million years ago, this massive dome survived ancient continental collisions. No spacecraft is required to see the ancient geology that illuminates the moon's blinding face. You
